description:
FILED s507c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) from #2704's probe table; PRE-EXISTING on main ac2fec1e.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3; scratch/s507c/m3/e3.pl in the s507c worktree):
  print "a[$}]\n";                 perl: a[]          PCL: a[$}]
  *{"main::}"} = \ "seven";
  print "b[$}]\n";                 perl: b[seven]     PCL: dies "Not a SCALAR reference" at the glob assignment
  print qq{c[$\}]}, "\n";          perl: c[seven]     PCL (after #2704): c[$}]
CAUSE: Pl/InterpScan.pm's $PUNCT_MAGIC has no `}` (nor `{`), so `$}` is not a reference start; and the symbolic glob `*{"main::}"}` does not resolve to the scalar slot.  `$}` is an unused perl variable -- this is the last row of #2704's table that still differs, nothing more.  Rare: no known program spells it.  If fixed, the emission needs a pipe-quoted symbol for the name (Pl::CLForm::needs_pipes) and the scanner change must be probed in REGEX mode too (`/a$}/`).
subject: The punctuation variable `$}` is not a variable in PCL: `"[$}]"` prints the literal `$}` (perl interpolates it, empty), so `qq{[$\}]}` (the escaped delimiter after a sigil, #2704) prints `[$}]` where perl prints `[]`; and `*{"main::}"} = \"seven"; print "$}"` dies "Not a SCALAR reference" (LOW, PRE-EXISTING, found by s507c)
